_meta.generatedBy: hand written from manufacturer installation drawings
_meta.provenance: Positions are per model, not from a general rule, and each point says where its figures come from in `provenance` (drawing, site, inferred, uncertain; null is not yet classified) with `basis` where they are not all one — docs/decisions.md D21. Coordinates are relative to that appliance's opening: x from the left side panel (left as you face it; in a neighbour's cabinet, from the side that meets the appliance — D22, round 70), y up from the opening floor, z either the rear wall or the front edge. A model with no entry here falls back to the room's generic rough-in heights and is marked as such under ?debug=1.

whenNoCabinet.basis: Sheet p. 4: where the construction makes a socket in an adjacent cabinet impossible, the appliance may be connected to an outlet behind it (B), and that alternative is permissible only if the outlet can be switched off at a circuit breaker. Behind the appliance is the drawing's; across the middle and 6" up are not, and put it in the routing area (B) the same drawing gives at the back of the opening.

points.basis: In an adjacent cabinet is on the drawing (A, recommended). 6" in and 6" up — near the floor — are not, and nor is which side of that cabinet the 6" is from. Measured from the side that meets the refrigerator (round 70): the drawing's sketch puts the socket just past the opening's side wall, and near the machine is what "adjacent" is for; it also keeps the socket by the refrigerator when the cabinet on the other side is the one taken.
